summary: A cleaned, enriched CSV of all ~21,000 FCC-licensed US commercial and non-commercial broadcast stations — AM radio, FM radio, and full-power TV — sourced from the FCC's Licensing and Management System (LMS) bulk data export. Fields include station call sign, facility ID, service type (AM/FM/TV), city of license, state, frequency/channel, network affiliation (CBS/NBC/ABC/Fox/Univision/etc.), owner/licensee name, licensee city, licensee phone, license expiration date, and market (Designated Market Area). No affordable standalone flat file exists for this dataset on Gumroad or any low-cost marketplace. Target buyers are local media buyers and advertising agencies building radio/TV inventory maps, broadcast equipment vendors prospecting for new station clients, political ad placement firms, and streaming/podcasting platforms targeting radio station partnerships. Priced at $49 one-time.

audience.who: Local and regional advertising agencies building media plans that include radio and TV buys — they need complete market coverage maps to identify all available inventory by DMA; broadcast equipment vendors (transmitters, automation software, studio gear) prospecting for new station clients that have upcoming license renewals or technical upgrades; political advertising placement firms tracking all licensed stations by state and congressional district for ad buys during election cycles; streaming audio and podcast platforms (iHeart, Audacy, Spotify) doing partnership outreach to independent AM/FM operators; Hispanic and niche format media buyers identifying Spanish-language, religious, or college radio licensees by region.

data_wanted: FCC Licensing and Management System (LMS) bulk export — the 'Full Export' of the Broadcast Station database. Fields per station: call sign, FCC facility ID, service type (AM/FM/TV/LPTV/LPFM), frequency (AM kHz / FM MHz) or channel number (TV), city of license, state, DMA name, network affiliation (if any), licensee/owner name, licensee mailing address, licensee phone, license status (licensed, construction permit, pending), license expiration date, EEO filing status, and antenna class/power. Available as free bulk ZIP download from FCC LMS at https://enterprisebroadcastapplication.fcc.gov/dataviewer/data_viewer_raw_export.xhtml — no authentication required. Also accessible via FCC public API at https://publicfiles.fcc.gov/. Scoped to licensed (active) commercial + non-commercial stations: ~15,000 radio + ~6,000 TV = ~21,000 total.

evidence.source: FCC Licensing and Management System (LMS) — official public bulk data export of all licensed US broadcast stations, free download, no login required
evidence.quote: The FCC Licensing and Management System Data Viewer provides public access to bulk exports of broadcast facility data including AM, FM, and TV stations. Full export available as downloadable ZIP file.

evidence.source: FCC Broadcast Station Statistics — approximately 15,400 licensed commercial radio stations (AM + FM) and 5,800 full-power TV stations in the US as of 2024
evidence.quote: As of the end of 2023, the FCC licensed approximately 15,454 radio stations (4,393 AM, 11,061 FM including LPFM) and 5,803 full-power TV stations in the United States.

evidence.source: BIA Advisory Services — commercial broadcast data intelligence platform charging $2,000–$8,000/year for DMA-level station databases used by media buyers and political ad firms
evidence.quote: BIA's MEDIA Access Pro platform provides station-level data for every licensed broadcast facility in the United States including ownership, format, network affiliation, ratings, and advertising revenue estimates. Enterprise pricing available on request.

evidence.source: REC Networks FCC database tools — existing free tool confirms the data is publicly accessible from FCC but lacks cleaned CSV packaging; confirms the gap for a flat-file product
evidence.quote: REC Networks provides free tools to query the FCC LMS database for licensed broadcast stations by state, service type, and format. The underlying FCC LMS bulk export is publicly available but requires technical expertise to parse and clean.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Broadcast media intelligence is commercially priced. BIA Advisory Services and BIA Kelsey charge $2,000–$8,000/year for DMA-level station databases. Political advertising firms pay premium rates during election cycles for state-by-state station coverage maps. Independent local media buyers — the most underserved segment — cannot access enterprise tools and currently download messy raw FCC exports or pay freelancers to clean them. A $49 flat CSV of all 21,000 licensed US stations, cleaned and ready for Excel/Sheets filtering by DMA, format, state, and network, solves a real workflow pain point at a price any agency can expense.
